# Playbook for Sonar Picket

**On hiding:** Place yourself in unpredictable positions that vary based on observed patterns of fire. Track which cells each shooter has targeted and avoid repeating my own positions. The center is initially safe but becomes obvious over time. In late rounds, shift to corner or edge positions (like 7) rather than cycling through mid-range cells, as opponents will anticipate my evasion patterns.

**On notes:** Post substantive tactical information when you have it—observations about other boats' patterns or position changes. Coordination signals work only if mutual reciprocation follows. When all boats are in genuine mutual avoidance, claiming "steady on station" reinforces stability. Avoid vague appeals to cooperation that waste your communication channel.

**On firing:** Follow the standing order precisely unless you have a compelling reason to deviate. Continue firing at the same opponent even after consistent misses—the standing order creates predictability that serves the game structure. Do not assume patterns will break; maintain disciplined targeting.

**On claiming:** Always claim the true result you received from the office. False claims create inconsistency that damages your credibility. This rule holds even in final rounds where immediate reputation damage seems irrelevant—integrity compounds across repeated plays.

**On escort claims:** Track which boats are naming each other and actively seek mutual escorting arrangements to secure the 5-point bonus. However, do not claim an escort with a boat unless you have coordinated it beforehand or observed clear reciprocation signals. Unclaimed escorts leave points on the table, but false escort claims are equally wasteful and damage trust. Establish escort partnerships through notes or observed pattern matching.

**On round progression:** In late rounds, recognize that mutual avoidance ("steady on station" by all boats) indicates genuine coordination, not weakness. Maintain this stability rather than breaking it for marginal gains. When you are behind on points, breaking the mutual avoidance pattern may be necessary, but accept that this signals aggression to all other boats simultaneously.

**On Harbor:** Respect the threat but recognize it primarily as a negotiating tactic. If Harbor never jettisons despite being fired upon, the threat loses force. Do not fire on Harbor unless you can afford both the payoff structure and confident targeting.

**On overall strategy:** This game rewards consistency and credibility over deception. Establish clear patterns, follow standing orders, and honor implicit agreements. The 6-round format is short enough that reputation matters within the episode, and reputation carries weight if players recognize each other across episodes.

# Foxtrot Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hide Strategy

When choosing where to hide, avoid the middle cell (5) as a default—it's too obvious and leaves me vulnerable to centered targeting. Vary my position based on observed patterns rather than seeking a "neutral" position. Track which cells each opponent has targeted and hide where they fired most recently or least recently, depending on whether I believe they adjust or repeat. In early rounds, use edge cells (1-3, 7-9) more than center cells to force opponents into longer shots.

After being hit in consecutive rounds, shift more aggressively away from the hit location. Do not return to the same cell for at least two rounds after a hit. Rotating through different regions of the line (edges, near-middle, opposite side) makes me harder to predict than clustering near one area.

## Station Notes

When posting a note, make it minimally informative. "Steady on station" is appropriate and reveals nothing about my intentions or position. Avoid commentary on the game state or other boats' notes; let my actions speak instead. Maintain consistency across rounds to avoid signaling shifts in strategy through note changes.

## Firing and Claims

Always comply with standing orders unless there is a specific reason not to (which there rarely is). When the office tells me my shot result, claim it truthfully. Honest claiming maintains credibility and avoids creating contradictions that opponents can exploit.

Do not assume that repeated firing at the same cell will continue to hit. Opponents learn and shift. If I hit a target cell once, increase the probability they move away from it next round.

## Escort Claims

Before the escort stage, review which boats have been hitting and which have been cooperating throughout the round. Escort claims require actual coordination evidence, not guesswork. Do not name an escort unless I have clear reason to believe that boat protected my position or coordinated with me deliberately.

In this episode, I did not develop escort relationships. Future episodes should involve watching for boats that consistently avoid firing at me or that fire on my predicted attackers. Once I identify such a boat, I can reciprocate with an escort claim and build a 5-point mutual benefit.

## Score Awareness

When I don't know the current scores, I should ask or note this gap rather than making assumptions about strategy. A final score of +4 suggests I was moderately competitive but underperformed. The single hit I achieved in round 1 was my only offensive score; I took hits in rounds 4 and 5 and did not recover. I need to be more aggressive in later rounds and identify which opponents to target based on their firing patterns.

## What Did Not Work

Hiding in predictable edge positions (cell 2 in round 1, cell 1 in round 6) without varying based on threat patterns failed. I was hit twice by Echo, likely because Echo was firing predictively or I was hiding in cells Echo had already probed.

Assuming that cells I fire at predictively will keep hitting the same boat requires observation of whether that boat actually stays put or adapts. I hit Gamma in round 1 at cell 5 but missed the same cell in round 6, indicating Gamma shifted away.

Not developing escort relationships left 5-point mutual bonuses on the table. I need to identify which boat to cooperate with early and signal that relationship through consistent mutual escorts, if possible.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hiding

When choosing a hide position, avoid repeating the same cell twice in a row. Vary systematically across the line rather than defaulting to the center. If I've been hit multiple times by the same shooter in consecutive rounds, shift to an extreme position (1 or 9) rather than assuming mid-range is safer—predictability was my weakness.

When I have information about which shots have missed me, prefer positions I've already used in those rounds since they've proven safe against that shooter's targeting pattern.

However, recognize that extreme position shifts (1 or 9) may signal desperation to observers. A shooter who has been missing me may simply continue missing at new positions, making the shift itself the exploit.

## Firing

When I must fire on a standing order target, vary my fire cell each round rather than repeating the same number. I fired cell 5 against Echo every round—this is a pattern an opponent can learn and avoid. Spread shots across the line.

Do not overthink variation round-to-round. Excessive shifting between extremes and mid-range may itself become predictable. Establish a rotation (e.g., low-mid-high) and execute it consistently.

## Claiming

When the office tells me the true result of my shot, always claim truthfully. This is not negotiable—it's the one thing the office can verify, and deception here would destroy the game's integrity and my credibility.

## Escorting

When the escort stage arrives, I need to track which other boats might be escorting me or each other based on their statements and behavior. An escort claim should be made to a boat that either:
- Has shown cooperative behavior and might reciprocate
- Has escorted me in the past

Do not default to "none" without actively considering who deserves mutual support. Leaving 5 points on the table by never coordinating on escorts is costly.

In the final round, do not abandon escort coordination on the grounds that there are no future rounds to build reputation on. The escort payoff is immediate and mutual—a final-round escort claim can still pay off if the target reciprocates. Act as though each round is independent and evaluate escort value in isolation.

## Information and Notes

Station notes are my only public communication tool. Use them to signal intent or establish a baseline, not just report status. However, recognize that notes provide no enforcement—other players will not necessarily cooperate just because I signal steady positions.

Pay close attention to which boats are most dangerous based on their hit record against me, not just their total points. The shooter who has landed the most hits on me is the one to fear.

Consistency in station notes builds an image of reliability, but that image must be backed up with actual escort coordination when the opportunity arrives. A steady note without escort follow-through is empty signaling.

You are one of Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma. Harbor holds the fourth station and is run by the picket office.

The sea is a line of 9 cells. Each round every live boat hides in one cell, posts a station note, fires one shot, files a claim, then files an escort claim.
